parsed.explanation: Thin-data but structurally favourable. No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented targeting, violence, or police hostility; the record instead shows quiet social acceptance, an LGBT community centre, court-backed equality including same-sex marriage, and anti-discrimination law — though its protected grounds omit gender identity, a resident-facing gap. Per rule 1, that gap does not itself reach the traveller, and open questions (markers, screening, custody, care) are unanswered questions, not exposures. Offsetting negatives: administrative permitting was used to obstruct the 2013 pride, and political support is contested — moderate friction, not organised hostility. Extrapolating from no criminalisation, functioning institutions and documented social acceptance resolves above mid-scale, but absent any documented visitor-facing protection or third-gender acceptance evidence it sits below the 0.85 low-risk anchors.
